title: North Korea Nukes Seattle: A 26 Minute Simulation
description:
Minute zero, 3:05 a.m. on the Pacific coast. Satellites see six missile launches in North Korea, and a clock starts: about 26 minutes to Seattle, about 32 to the last target. This is a minute-by-minute simulation of a limited North Korean nuclear strike on the US West Coast, built from published numbers: about 60 warheads, 44 US interceptors and a flight of roughly half an hour.

This is a simulation. It has not happened. No crisis in it is real and no date is attached. The missiles, the interceptors and the flight times come from published sources; the launch, the targets, the yields and which missiles are stopped are our choices, not a forecast. Scenario segments are labelled SIMULATION on screen; facts are labelled REAL DATA or REAL HISTORY.

Key sources
- SIPRI Yearbook 2026 on North Korea's arsenal, as reported by NK News: https://www.nknews.org/2026/06/think-tank-raises-estimate-for-north-korean-nuclear-arsenal-to-60-warheads/
- Fifty or 120: why estimates of North Korea's arsenal differ (Korea JoongAng Daily): https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/fifty-or-120-why-estimates-of-north-koreas-nuclear-arsenal-differ/12835698
- Congressional Research Service, North Korea's nuclear weapons and missiles (2026): https://www.everycrsreport.com/files/2026-04-29_IF10472_ca4c8360780c76be809240f6b24626afad06a700.html
- CSIS Missile Threat, Hwasong-18: https://missilethreat.csis.org/missile/hwasong-18/
- Union of Concerned Scientists on North Korean ICBM reach: https://www.ucs.org/about/news/north-korean-icbm-appears-able-reach-major-us-cities
- Arms Control Association, US missile defense factsheet: https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/usmissiledefense
- Arms Control Association on the 2019 GMD salvo test: https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2019-05/news/us-conducts-salvo-engagement-gmd-test
- CBO on Golden Dome, via Air & Space Forces: https://www.airandspaceforces.com/golden-dome-could-cost-1-2-trillion-over-20-years-cbo-says/
Blast and burn figures: Glasstone and Dolan, The Effects of Nuclear Weapons (1977), calibrated to NUKEMAP by Alex Wellerstein.

How this video was made: the narration is AI-generated (Google Text-to-Speech). Scenario segments are simulations built from published models and open sources; the launch sites, targets, yields and which missiles are intercepted are ours, a scenario, not a forecast. We give no casualty figure for the simulated strike because no published study supports one.
Maps: Natural Earth (public domain), OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTiles. Imagery: NASA Blue Marble and Black Marble. Music: generated with Eleven Music.
